name: Roland S-330
source: Roland S-330 Owner's Manual, MIDI Implementation 'Date: Jun. 12 1988, Version 1.00' (printed pp.149-159: chart, Roland exclusive/handshake procedures, S-330 section 3 exclusive communications, section 4 address map 4.1-4.6), panel chapters pp.70-96 (tone parameters), 114 (initial values), 116-119 (MIDI mode), 162 (specifications); https://static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/S-330_OM.pdf (scanned, read from 220 dpi renders). Cross-checked against audiocontrol (github.com/audiocontrol-org/audiocontrol, Apache-2.0, Orion Letizi) modules/sampler-devices/src/devices/s330 + roland-s-series + docs/1.0/s330-sysex-protocol.md, and its hardware captures test/fixtures/s330/*.ndjson (fetch-tone-0 and load-everything captured from a real S-330; most write fixtures are S-550). Offsets below are the manual's nibble addresses (linear 7-bit units), not audiocontrol's de-nibbled byte offsets (= offset / 2).

roland.checksum: Roland: (128 - (sum of address + data bytes (DT1/DAT) or address + size bytes (RQ1/RQD/WSD)) % 128) % 128. Hardware-captured examples (dev 00): RQD tone T11 F0 41 00 1E 41 00 03 00 00 00 00 02 00 7B F7 (audiocontrol asks 00 00 04 00 = two tones, sum 79); WSD one patch param F0 41 00 1E 40 00 00 03 5A 00 00 00 02 21 F7; its DAT F0 41 00 1E 42 00 00 03 5A 06 04 19 F7 (patch P11 level = 100 = nibbles 6,4).

messageFormat.RQ1: F0 41 <dev> 1E 11 <a1 a2 a3 a4> <s1 s2 s3 s4> <sum> F7 -- answered with DT1(s) 'only when the recognized address and size match'; illegal address/size is silently ignored (manual 3.1.1). Verified on a real S-330 by audiocontrol's roland-handshake-diag (RQ1 00 00 00 00 size 00 00 00 04 -> DT1 in 18 ms)
messageFormat.handshake: WSD 40 / RQD 41 / DAT 42 / ACK 43 / EOD 45 / ERR 4E / RJC 4F, same address+size fields; see driverNotes 'handshake'

roland.deviceId: dev = panel Device ID - 1 (MIDI > Message > Device ID 1-16 -> 00-0F; factory 1 -> 00). NOT 10h like the D-110/JV.
roland.addressing: 4 address bytes of 7 bits (00-7F each). An 'address unit' is one transmitted MIDI byte. PARAMETER DATA IS NIBBLED: every logical 8-bit value occupies 2 address units, '0000 aaaa' then '0000 bbbb' (value = aaaa<<4 | bbbb); the 24-bit wave points occupy 6 units (MSB nibble first). So param.offset here = the manual's offset address (linear: 01 06 = 134), and every param has size 2 (or 6); rolandDriver's existing size>1 nibble path (high nibble first) reads/writes these unchanged. Addresses and sizes must be even (manual *3-1: lowest bit of the LSB of address and size = 0; *3-2: even number of data bytes). Wave data (01 xx xx xx) is NOT nibbled: 2 units per 12-bit sample, see waveTransfer.

tone.desc: Tone parameters of the EDIT TARGET tone. Tone n (0-31 = T11..T48) lives at 00 03 (2n) 00, 00 00 02 00 units (128 logical bytes). The S-330 has no temporary/edit-buffer area: this IS the tone in RAM, and edits are heard immediately on any patch that maps the tone. base here = T11; the driver must move it to the selected tone (driverNotes 1).

patch.desc: Patch parameters, P11 (patch p at 00 00 (4p) 00, 00 00 04 00 units = 256 logical bytes; P11-P18 = p 0-7, P21-P28 = 8-15). Context only (notInPatch): bend range, key mode, two 109-key tone-to-key maps, level, output. Name (12 chars at 00 00-00 17) is left unmodelled so it doesn't join the tone-name field.

function.desc: Function parameters 00 01 00 00 (whole area is 00 00 08 00 units; this schema reads the first 00 00 00 66: master tune, voice mode, voice group A-H RX channel / patch / level). Also in the area: block-1 disk label 00 66-01 5D (60 chars), OUTPUT MODE at 05 5E (0 individual, 1 mix). Context only.

otherAreas.midi: 00 02 00 00, 00 00 04 00 units: RX CHANNEL 1-8 at 00 40-00 4F (0-15 = ch 1-16, 16 = OFF); RX PROGRAM CHANGE 1-8 at 00 50; RX BENDER at 00 60; RX MODULATION at 00 70; RX HOLD at 01 00; RX AFTER TOUCH at 01 10; RX VOLUME at 01 20; RX BEND RANGE at 01 30 (each 8 x 2 units, 0 OFF / 1 ON); SYSTEM EXCLUSIVE at 01 42 (0 OFF / 1 ON); DEVICE ID at 01 44 (0-15); RX PROGRAM CHANGE NUMBER 1-32 at 01 46-02 07 (0-127, the Prog # table; the panel shows 16 entries, P11-P28). Deliberately NOT modelled as params: a DT1 of SYSTEM EXCLUSIVE = OFF or a new DEVICE ID cuts the editor off.
otherAreas.sw: 00 04 00 00, 00 00 00 08 units (manual 4.5): SW1 (all), SW2 (character), SW3 (patch), ALPHA DIAL -127..+127. audiocontrol found (undocumented, hardware-tested) that DT1s here press front-panel buttons: F0 41 dev 1E 12 00 04 00 00 <cat> <code> <sum> F7 -- cat 09 = arrows/INC/DEC (press 00-05: right, left, up, down, INC, DEC; release = press + 08), cat 01 = MODE 0B, MENU 0C, SUB MENU 0D, COM 0E, EXECUTE 0F; e.g. EXECUTE F0 41 00 1E 12 00 04 00 00 01 0F 6C F7. The S-330 also transmits these when its own buttons are pressed.
otherAreas.wave: 01 00 00 00 wave bank A x 18 segments, 01 20 00 00 wave bank B x 18 (see waveTransfer)
otherAreas.gaps: 00 00 40 00-00 00 7F 7F answers RQD with blank patch-shaped data (audiocontrol reads 64 'patches'; the manual and spec say 16 -- only 00 00 00 00-00 00 3C 00 are real). Request bytes >= 80h are invalid MIDI data and get RJC/garbage.

encodings.nibble: size 2 (one logical byte) or 6 (24-bit point): value = concatenation of the low 4 bits of each unit, MSB first. Existing driver path.
encodings.twos: NEW (driverNotes 2): signed values (-64..+63, -24..+24, -2..+2, tone-to-key -1 = OFF) are the logical byte in two's complement. read: raw = nibble value; v = raw >= 128 ? raw - 256 : raw. write: raw = v & 255, then nibble-split. Evidence: the manual prints tone-to-key '-1: OFF', and a real S-330 dump holds 0 for master tune / fine tune / LFO offset / patch detune / octave shift, whose factory defaults are 0 (offset-binary would read 64/2).

roland.timing: One-way (RQ1/DT1): the manual asks >= 20 ms between DT1 messages. Handshake: audiocontrol waits 500 ms for each ACK, retries 3x with 100 ms x2 backoff (max 2 s), flushes coalesced parameter writes every 150 ms, and waits 500 ms after a wave upload before the next command. Captured round trips: ACK to WSD ~15 ms; each 128-unit DAT + its ACK ~61 ms.
roland.notes: No ROM: the OS boots from floppy, and all tones/patches/waves are RAM loaded from a sound disk. Nothing written over MIDI survives power-off unless saved on the panel (DISK > Save). 16 patches (P11-P28), 32 tones (T11-T48), 2 x 18 wave segments, 8 voice groups A-H each with its own RX channel + patch (Multi). Exclusive is OFF at power-up by default (it is part of the MIDI setup saved on the system disk). The S-330 transmits DT1 when a tone parameter is edited on its panel and when it answers RQ1; it never sends RQ1/WSD/RQD itself.

params.name: Output Assign
params.note: which individual output jack when the patch's Output Assign = TONE

params.name: Source (Original) Tone
params.note: the tone whose wave data this tone plays (itself for an ORG tone)

params.name: Orig / Sub Tone
params.note: ORG owns wave memory; SUB borrows the Source Tone's wave data (manual p.71)

params.name: Sampling Frequency
params.note: how the stored samples are played back; changing it re-pitches the wave, it does not resample

params.name: Original Key
params.note: MIDI note 11-108; key that plays the sample at recorded pitch. Factory init C5 (72). The S-330 can play at most 2 octaves above this

params.name: Wave Segment Top
params.note: first 0.4 s (12000-sample) segment of the bank this tone owns

params.name: Wave Segment Length
params.note: number of segments owned; 0 = no wave (deleted/sub tone)

params.name: Start Point
params.note: 24-bit sample index relative to the segment top (6 nibbles, MSB first). Real dump: a 2-segment tone ends at 23999

params.name: End Point
params.note: 24-bit, relative to segment top. Keep loopLength = endPoint - loopPoint (see driverNotes)

params.name: Loop Point
params.note: 24-bit, relative to segment top. Keep loopLength = endPoint - loopPoint (see driverNotes)

params.name: TVA LFO Depth
params.note: 00 34: the map prints 'TVA LFO DEPTH' here AND at 00 42; audiocontrol treats 00 34 as TVA. See uncertain

params.name: LFO Sync
params.note: ON = LFO restarts at zero phase on each note

params.name: LFO Mode
params.note: labels as printed in the address map; the panel chapter has no one-shot LFO. See uncertain

params.name: Pitch LFO Depth
params.note: 00 42: printed 'TVA LFO DEPTH' (duplicate); taken to be the panel's P. LFO Depth. See uncertain

params.name: LFO Wave (Sine / Peak Hold)
params.note: printed 'LFO POLALITY 0 Sine 1 Peak hold' = the panel's LFO Mode Sin/P.H. See uncertain

params.name: LFO Offset
params.note: -64..+63, two's complement byte (see driverNotes 'twos')

params.name: Pitch Shift
params.note: panel: Shift -24..+24 semitones, used when Pitch Follow is OFF; the map prints 0-127. Two's complement assumed

params.name: Fine Tune
params.note: +-50 ~ half a semitone (manual p.72)

programs.note: The edit focus is a TONE. Tone banks T1x-T4x are the 32 RAM tones (no ROM, no presets); selecting one only changes which tone the editor reads and edits (no MIDI goes out; driverNotes 1). Patch banks are backup-only (PC selects which patch a voice group plays; the editor reads/writes patches as raw 512-unit blocks). No bank select: CC0/32 are not recognised.

areas.what: function (multi setup, disk label, output mode)
MIDI setup (rx switches, exclusive, device ID, Prog # table)
wave data banks A and B
areas.rq1: not a parameter backup: RQD 01 00 00 00 / 01 20 00 00 per segment (waveTransfer); ~3.5 min per bank

backup.notInSysex: The OS itself, disk directory and anything on the floppy. Restoring tones without their wave data leaves tones pointing at whatever wave memory holds.
backup.restore: DT1 (or WSD) the saved blocks back to the same addresses, >= 20 ms apart; restore wave data first, then tones, then patches, then function. Then save to disk on the panel.

setup: Boot first: the S-330 has no OS in ROM. Put an S-330 System Disk image (not an S-50/S-550 one) on the Gotek, power on, let it load, then load a sound disk (or start empty). Without the OS the unit does nothing on MIDI.
Cable both ways: interface out -> S-330 MIDI IN, S-330 MIDI OUT -> interface in. RQ1 answers and handshake ACKs need the return path.
MODE > MIDI > Message: Exclusive = ON (factory default is OFF), Device ID = 1 (the editor's default device 00). Match any other Device ID in the editor.
Same page: voice group A RX-CH = the editor's channel (factory A = ch 1, B-H = 2-8). P.Chg ON for group A if you want the patch banks to switch patches.
To hear the tone you edit, the patch on group A (factory P11) must map it: in EDIT > Split (or via this editor's keymap params) set layer-1 tone-to-key for the keys you play to that tone.
Stay in PLAY or EDIT mode while the editor works. The sampling screen ignores remote messages, and pressing ENTER/EXECUTE on the panel during a transfer aborts it with RJC.
Save to disk when done (DISK > Save): SysEx edits live only in RAM. Save the MIDI setup to the system disk if you want Exclusive ON at the next boot.
driverNotes: rolandDriver fits the S-330's one-way protocol (RQ1/DT1, 4-byte address + size, Roland checksum, nibbled data via the existing size>1 path) but needs these changes. (1) EDIT TARGET FOLLOWS THE SELECTED TONE (required): the S-330 has no edit buffer, so the 'tone' block must be re-based to the chosen RAM tone. For a bank whose select.type is 'slot', programChange(bi, prog) sends NO MIDI; it sets blockOf(select.block).at = toInt(userMemory[bank.memory].base) + prog * stride, resets mirror[block] (so a stale mirror is never DT1'd into another tone), and remembers the slot (prefs, key 'slot'; makeDriver would need to pass prefs to rolandDriver) so the next connect's requestPatch reads the same tone. requestPatch/sendParam/sendPatch/decode then all use the moved base. requestProgram/writeProgram/requestSlotName already address slots via userMemory and need no change. (2) ENCODING 'twos': in read(), after the nibble join, if p.encoding === 'twos' return raw >= 1 << (4*size - 1) ? raw - (1 << 4*size) : raw; in write(), start from v & ((1 << 4*size) - 1). Params keep negative min (e.g. -64) so the editor's clamp/knob work as-is. (3) NAMES ARE NIBBLED: requestName() and requestSlotName() currently take r.data[p.offset] raw, which is only the high nibble here. Use read(p, r.data) and request Math.max(offset + width) units (16 for the tone name). nameFrom() (raw slots with no modelled block, i.e. patch backups) should de-nibble the first 24 units into 12 chars when R.addressing is nibbled, e.g. a schema flag roland.nibbled = true. (4) DERIVED LOOP LENGTH: loopLength (01 4C) must equal endPoint - loopPoint (a real S-330 dump: 23999 - 8778 = 15221). After a send of endPoint or loopPoint, also send loopLength (6 units). Suggested schema hook: param.derived = { key: 'loopLength', from: 'endPoint - loopPoint' } handled in sendParam/sendPatch; until then, sendPatch after any point edit writes the stale value. (5) RANDOMIZE SAFETY: wave pointer/point params are norandom, but sendPatch before a successful requestPatch would DT1 zeros over a real tone (mirror starts empty). Refuse sendPatch/writeProgram for the tone block until it has been read once. (6) CONTEXT BLOCKS: 'patch' (P11, 512 units) and 'function' (102 units) are read after each requestPatch (existing contextBlocks path, ~0.3 s extra) and only sent per param. Optional: re-base 'patch' to the patch playing on voice group A (function multiPatch1) so the patch controls follow the unit. (7) PROTOCOL CHOICE: the manual documents both one-way (RQ1/DT1, 'suited to small amounts of data', >= 20 ms between DT1s, DT1 <= 256 data bytes, RQ1 answered only for a legal address/size, silently ignored otherwise) and handshake. RQ1 is hardware-verified (audiocontrol diag, real S-330); DT1 parameter writes are per the manual and audiocontrol's DT1 panel remote at 00 04 00 00 works, but audiocontrol's own writes all use WSD, and its code comments that WSD is 'the ONLY method that works for function parameter writes'. First hardware test: DT1 one tone param (e.g. TVF cutoff F0 41 00 1E 12 00 03 00 4C 03 0C 22 F7 for T11 = 60) and read it back with RQ1 F0 41 00 1E 11 00 03 00 4C 00 00 00 02 2F F7. If DT1 is ignored, implement the handshake below as transport 'rolandHandshake' (same schema). (8) HANDSHAKE STATE MACHINES (manual 3.2 / Roland section 4, and audiocontrol's hardware-tested client). READ: host RQD F0 41 dev 1E 41 <addr4> <size4> <sum> F7 (size in address units: tone 00 00 02 00, patch 00 00 04 00) -> device RJC F0 41 dev 1E 4F F7 (illegal address/size, not ready, operator pressed ENTER) OR a DAT F0 41 dev 1E 42 <addr4> <data> <sum> F7 (128 units per packet observed, address advancing 00 00 01 00 per packet; sum covers addr+data) -> host ACK F0 41 dev 1E 43 F7 after EVERY DAT (the device will not send the next one without it) -> ... -> device EOD F0 41 dev 1E 45 F7 -> host ACK. Bad checksum: host sends ERR F0 41 dev 1E 4E F7, device resends that DAT or answers RJC and stops; host may send RJC to abort. WRITE: host WSD F0 41 dev 1E 40 <addr4> <size4> <sum> F7 -> device ACK (or RJC) -> host DAT (<= 128 units, addresses contiguous, sum over addr+data) -> device ACK per DAT -> host EOD -> device ACK (audiocontrol: the S-330 sometimes never ACKs the EOD of a parameter or wave write; treat 300-500 ms of silence after EOD as success, then read back). Non-contiguous DAT addresses or ERR => device RJC. Stale RJC/ACK from an earlier timed-out exchange can arrive late: audiocontrol ignores RJC mid-exchange and relies on its 500 ms ACK timeout plus retries. One exchange at a time (serialize), and single params can be WSD'd at their own address with size 00 00 00 02 (captured on the S-550: WSD 00 00 03 5A size 2, DAT 06 04). (9) DEVICE ID default 00 (panel 1), set via roland.defaultDeviceId = 0 (the driver's '?? 16' fallback keeps 0). A per-device prefs override like the Yamaha driver's would help, since Device ID is a panel setting. (10) decode(): the S-330 transmits DT1 when a tone parameter is edited on its panel, so decode works for the selected tone once (1) is in; edits to other tones fall outside the block and are ignored.

waveTransfer.summary: Wave memory is directly addressable: WSD/RQD (or, untested, DT1/RQ1) at 01 xx xx xx moves raw 12-bit samples in and out; a tone then points at them. Not nibbled, 2 units per sample, ~2 KB/s over the handshake -- about 29x slower than real time.
waveTransfer.memory: 512k words total (spec). Bank A at 01 00 00 00, bank B at 01 20 00 00; each 18 segments; segment s of a bank at bank base + s * 24576 units (00 01 40 00, the manual's per-segment 'Total size'), 7-bit linear: bank A seg 1 = 01 01 40 00, seg 12 = 01 12 00 00, seg 17 = 01 19 40 00; bank B seg 0 = 01 20 00 00. (audiocontrol's doc table shows seg 1 as 01 00 40 00 -- that is an arithmetic slip; its code computes 01 01 40 00.) 24576 units = 12288 sample slots, but tones use 12000 samples per segment (0.4 s at 30 kHz; a real 2-segment tone ends at 23999; audiocontrol transfers 24000 bytes per segment). Total 36 segments = 14.4 s at 30 kHz or 28.8 s at 15 kHz.
waveTransfer.sampleFormat: 12-bit two's complement, mono, 2 units per sample: unit 0 = 0aaa aaaa (bits 11-5), unit 1 = 0bbb bb00 (bits 4-0 shifted left 2). encode: u = s12 & 0xFFF; b0 = (u >> 5) & 0x7F; b1 = (u << 2) & 0x7C. decode: v = (b0 << 5) | (b1 >> 2); if (v & 0x800) v -= 0x1000. From 16-bit PCM: s12 = clamp(round(s16 / 16), -2048, 2047) (truncating instead of rounding, and no dither, gives the grittier 12-bit sound).
waveTransfer.requestSize: RQD/WSD size = samples x 2 (units = bytes on the wire), e.g. one segment 24000 = 00 01 3B 40 (7-bit). Address LSB and size must be even.
waveTransfer.upload: WSD F0 41 dev 1E 40 <seg address> <size> <sum> F7 -> ACK -> DAT packets of 128 bytes, each F0 41 dev 1E 42 <addr of this chunk = start + 128k> <128 bytes> <sum> F7, wait for ACK before the next (audiocontrol waits 10 ms after the WSD ACK and 5 ms after each DAT ACK) -> EOD -> ACK (may never come; 500 ms silence = done). Then wait ~500 ms: the S-330 is busy committing and ignores WSD meanwhile.
waveTransfer.download: RQD <seg address> <samples x 2> -> DAT (128 bytes each) / ACK ... EOD / ACK. On the S-550 only even segments could be read back (odd ones RJC though they accept writes); not verified on the S-330.
waveTransfer.speed: MIDI wire max 3125 bytes/s. Measured handshake cadence ~61 ms per 128-byte DAT+ACK (~2.1 KB/s, ~1050 samples/s): one 12000-sample segment ~11-12 s, a full bank ~3.5 min, all 36 segments ~7 min.
waveTransfer.toneSetup: audiocontrol importTone order: (1) write the tone block first (ORG: origSub 0, sourceTone = itself, samplingFreq, waveBank, waveSegTop, waveSegLen = ceil(samples / 12000), startPoint 0, endPoint = samples - 1, loopPoint, loopLength = endPoint - loopPoint, loopMode, origKey, pitchFollow ON, level 127), (2) upload the wave, (3) wait 500 ms, (4) write the tone block again (params sent after the wave are what take effect reliably). Never let two ORG tones' segment ranges overlap.
waveTransfer.crushPipeline: For 'send a folder of WAVs -> play -> record': per WAV, sum to mono, resample to 30000 Hz (or 15000 Hz for twice the time per segment and more aliasing), quantize to 12-bit, cut to <= 18 segments per bank (7.2 s at 30 kHz), allocate segment ranges across banks A/B (36 segments total per memory load, 32 tones max), upload + set up the tone as above, point a patch at it (layer-1 tone-to-key: all 109 keys = that tone, key mode NORMAL; group A plays the patch), then play notes at origKey on group A's channel and record the analog output (or the tone's individual output). Batch = fill memory, render every tone, reload the next batch. Budget ~12 s transfer per 0.4 s of 30 kHz audio.
gotchas: PLAY or EDIT mode only; the sampling screen ignores remote.
Pressing ENTER/EXECUTE on the panel during a transfer aborts it (RJC).
Wave uploads overwrite RAM immediately; they are lost at power-off unless saved to disk.
End points beyond the uploaded samples play whatever memory holds.

uncertain: DT1 parameter writes are documented by the manual but not hardware-verified on an S-330 by any source found; audiocontrol writes everything with WSD and states WSD is the only method that worked for function parameters. RQ1 reads ARE verified (small read at 00 00 00 00). Whether RQ1 accepts a whole-tone size (00 00 02 00) in one request, and how the reply is split, is untested -- the manual only says the S-330 answers when 'address and size match'.

Two's complement for signed params is inferred (tone-to-key '-1: OFF' in the manual; real dumps hold 0 where the factory default is 0). audiocontrol is inconsistent: two's complement for transpose/loop tune, offset-binary (64 / 2 = centre) for patch detune/octave shift and LFO offset 64 in its init tone.
Pitch Shift (transpose, 00 48): the map prints 0-127, the panel -24..+24. Modelled -24..+24 two's complement.

LFO depth addresses: the map prints 'TVA LFO DEPTH' at both 00 34 and 00 42; the panel has P. LFO Depth (Tone PRM), TVF LFO Depth (00 54) and TVA LFO Depth. Modelled 00 34 = TVA (audiocontrol's reading) and 00 42 = pitch. Test: rate ~60, set 00 42 to 127 -- vibrato means pitch; tremolo means they are swapped.

LFO mode/polarity: the map has 00 40 'LFO MODE 0 NORMAL 1 ONE SHOT' and 00 44 'LFO POLALITY 0 Sine 1 Peak hold'; the panel has Mode (Sin / Peak Hold) and Polarity (+ / -). 00 44 is modelled as the Sine/Peak-hold wave; whether 00 40 is really one-shot or the panel's +/- polarity is unknown.

Point units: start/end/loop are printed 0-221180/221184 (= 18 x 12288), but real tones use 12000 samples per segment (2-segment tone end = 23999) and audiocontrol's transfers assume 12000. Whether points address 12288-sample segments across a multi-segment tone (a gap every 288 samples) is unknown; keep tones inside the 12000 x N convention.

Patch count: the manual (address map 'x16', Multi patch 0-15, spec '16 Patch') says 16; audiocontrol's config says 64 and reads 32 addressable slots (00 00 40 00-00 00 7C 00 answer with blank data). Modelled 16.
TVA/TVF env: sustain printed 0-7, end 1-7 (8 level/rate pairs); audiocontrol's init tone writes end point 8. Level/rate numbering from the map.
Level curves (00 5A, 01 32) 0-5 and Env Zoom 0-5: shapes/meanings not described in the MIDI implementation.
Wave upload over one-way DT1 (instead of WSD) is unexplored; the handshake is the documented large-data path.
Patch 'COPY SOURCE' (03 56, printed 0-7) left unmodelled; meaning unclear.
Front-panel ROLL button is labelled PAGE on some units (photo) -- cosmetic, no MIDI effect.
